Real Love Must Be Lived Out

“Let us not love in word only, neither with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.”
1 John 3:18–24
3:18 Little children, let us not love in word only, neither with the tongue only, but in deed and truth. 3:19 And hereby we know that we are of the truth, and persuade our heart before him, 3:20 because if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and knows all things. 3:21 Beloved, if our heart doesn’t condemn us, we have boldness toward God; 3:22 and whatever we ask, we receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do the things that are pleasing in his sight. 3:23 This is his commandment, that we should believe in the name of his Son, Jesus Christ, and love one another, even as he commanded. 3:24 He who keeps his commandments remains in him, and he in him. By this we know that he remains in us, by the Spirit which he gave us.
John brings love from “saying” to “living”: “not in word only, neither with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.” True love is not just the words “I love you”; it is being willing to give when the other is in need, to forgive when hurt, and to lay oneself down first in conflict. Jesus is the most perfect example: he didn’t just tell us he loves us; on the cross he gave himself up and truly lived out that love. So a changed life must bring changed relationships; when Christ’s love enters us, it will surely flow from our lives to others.
But sometimes our own weakness makes us condemn ourselves, even doubting whether we are worthy to come before God. John comforts us: “God is greater than our heart.” Our feelings are not the final judge; God is. He fully knows our failures, and fully knows the grace we have received in Christ. So don’t keep being condemned by your feelings; turn your focus back to Jesus. When we come honestly before God and receive his light, forgiveness, and renewal, our hearts can be at rest again and come boldly before him.
In the end John boils the Christian life down to two things: “believe in Jesus” and “love one another.” Faith unites us with Christ, and love lets Christ’s life flow out of us. And this isn’t something we force ourselves to do, because God has given us the Holy Spirit. A true Christian life is led by the Holy Spirit, with Jesus reigning within, turning us from “caring only for ourselves” to loving God and people. Life first, then relationships; when Christ’s life fills us, love is no longer just a word but becomes a visible way of living.
“Let us not love in word only, neither with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.”
